cultural.vision_reason: The image shows a hand-woven strip-woven cotton skirt cloth with magenta (alaari silk) and indigo stripes, a traditional Nupe woman's garment construction technique well documented for this people.

physical.title: textile; skirt
physical.summary: Woman’s skirt composed of 22 narrow strips with two warp-faced patterns, hand-woven and hand-sewn together along the selvages; in addition there is a longer edging strip at the top of indigo-dyed cotton thread (with no patterning) which serves as a tie. All the thread is handspun. 19 of the strips have the same pattern, with a central band of magenta silk (alaari) thread flanked by two narrower bands of indigo-dyed cotto, and with two stripes of six threads of white cotton down the centre of the magenta band, while two threads of cotton separate the magenta from the indigo. The remaining 3 strips have a wide band of alaari silk and a narrow band of indigo, but no band of white cotton; these strips form a wide band of silk in the centre and another along the bottom edge, in such a way as to imitate a two-panel cloth of woman’s weave. The weft is of indigo, and the cloth has not been hemmed.
